## Features

What the system does. Each feature is proven at the levels it requires.

| Feature | What it does | `oss` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sql.join` | Inner, left, full outer and self joins, maintained incrementally. | ✅ |
| `sql.aggregate` | GROUP BY aggregates, HAVING, global aggregates and views over views. | ✅ |
| `sql.window` | Window functions (RANK and DENSE_RANK top-k, LAG, running SUM over a RANGE frame). | ✅ |
| `sql.tumble` | The TUMBLE table function for fixed event-time windows. | ✅ |
| `sql.hop` | The HOP table function for sliding event-time windows. | ✅ |
| `sql.subquery` | EXISTS, NOT EXISTS, IN, NOT IN and correlated scalar subqueries. | ✅ |
| `sql.setop` | UNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT, INTERSECT and DISTINCT. | ✅ |
| `connector.http` | HTTP ingress with completion tokens, and HTTP egress change streams with an optional snapshot. | ❌ |
| `connector.kafka` | Kafka input and output. Without fault tolerance, the output retries broker failures with no delivery deadline. | ✅ |
| `sql.grouping` | GROUP BY ROLLUP, CUBE and GROUPING SETS with GROUPING(). | ❌ |
| `sql.asof` | LEFT ASOF JOIN with a MATCH_CONDITION on timestamps. | ✅ |
| `sql.lateness` | LATENESS on timestamp columns, which lets Feldera discard state it no longer needs. | ✅ |
| `transactions` | start_transaction and commit_transaction group inputs so views update once, on commit. | ✅ |
| `sql.primary_key` | PRIMARY KEY tables, where inserts overwrite and updates change named columns (Uniqueness Constraints). | ✅ |
| `sql.recursion` | Mutually recursive views with least-fixed-point semantics (Mutually-Recursive Queries). | ✅ |
| `sql.now` | NOW() and temporal filters, re-evaluated on a step every clock_resolution (Date/time functions). | ✅ |
| `sql.adhoc` | Ad-hoc SELECT queries on materialized tables and views, answered by DataFusion (Ad-hoc SQL Queries). | ✅ |
| `sql.types` | Every SQL column type, encoded as JSON on HTTP and Kafka (SQL types, JSON format). | ✅ |
| `input.errors` | Rejection of malformed records on ingress (JSON format). | ✅ |
| `connector.postgres` | The PostgreSQL output connector in materialized mode (PostgreSQL output connector, experimental). | ✅ |
| `runtime.workers` | The workers setting runs a pipeline on that many threads. It can change only while storage is cleared (Pipeline configuration). | ❌ |
| `sql.type_semantics` | Equality, order and SUM for every SQL type inside stateful operators (Comparison Operations, Floating Point Operations, Array and Map comparisons, Aggregate Operations). | ❌ |

- <a id="inv-delivery.no_loss"></a>**`delivery.no_loss`** · safety · delivery — Every record read from the input topic reaches the output topic while the pipeline keeps running. ("temporary broker failures are retried without a delivery deadline", Kafka output connector.)
- <a id="inv-delivery.recovers"></a>**`delivery.recovers`** · liveness · delivery — After the last fault ends, the output catches up with the input within two minutes, and the pipeline stays Running.

### `types.operators`

Every Feldera SQL column type, the members of types.contract, inside each operator that keeps state. A supported answer means the operator's view equals the model at every step of three seeds of inserts and deletes, at 1, 4 and 8 workers. The model works from value classes: values the docs call equal share a class, and classes rank in the order the docs give. Deletes often name a row by another spelling of its value, such as "1.50" for 1.5. Unsupported means the compiler refuses the pair, or accepts it only by casting the value to another type.

## Exemptions and refusals

Each ☑️ and ⛔, with the reason and the test that proves it.

- `path.kafka_kafka` × `delivery.no_duplicates`: exempt. The docs promise no duplicates only across a graceful stop, which checkpoints. The community edition refuses a graceful stop (501 EnterpriseFeature), so the promise has nothing to apply to. Proven by `feldera.kafka/path.kafka_kafka/delivery.no_duplicates`.
- `path.kafka_kafka` × `faults.contract/process_kill`: unsupported. Recovery from a crash needs fault tolerance, which "is only available in Feldera Enterprise Edition" (Checkpoints & Fault Tolerance). The open-source pipeline restarts empty. Proven by `feldera.kafka/path.kafka_kafka/faults.contract/process_kill`.
- `path.kafka_kafka` × `faults.contract/stop_and_resume`: unsupported. A graceful stop (stop?force=false) "checkpoint[s] before compute is deprovisioned" (Pipeline lifecycle), but the community edition refuses it with 501 EnterpriseFeature and keeps running. Proven by `feldera.kafka/path.kafka_kafka/faults.contract/stop_and_resume`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/bool`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument (Aggregate Operations), and the compiler refuses BOOLEAN. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/bool`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/varchar`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument. The compiler accepts a string by casting it to a number, so the operator sums numbers, not strings. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/varchar`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/char`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument. The compiler accepts a string by casting it to a number, so the operator sums numbers, not strings. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/char`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/binary`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument (Aggregate Operations), and the compiler refuses BINARY(4). Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/binary`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/varbinary`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument (Aggregate Operations), and the compiler refuses VARBINARY. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/varbinary`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/date`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument (Aggregate Operations), and the compiler refuses DATE. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/date`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/time`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument (Aggregate Operations), and the compiler refuses TIME. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/time`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/ts`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument (Aggregate Operations), and the compiler refuses TIMESTAMP. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/ts`.
- `op.sum` × `types.operators/tstz`: unsupported. SUM takes a numeric argument (Aggregate Operations), and the compiler refuses TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE. Proven by `feldera.type_semantics_sum/op.sum/types.operators/tstz`.
